way Company to Manchoukuo from eleven cities and sixty-two towns and
villages in the S. M. R. Zone alone were estimated at 31,438,994 yen and
schools transfered to the Japanese authorities, 20,708,000 yen.
Together with this gigantic transfer, a total of nearly 14,000 persons,
including Japanese and Manchurians, had passed into the employment of
Manchoukuo, either directly or indirectly. Among them may be mentioned
1,396 police officers and men from the Japanese Embassy, 3,723 police
officers and men from the Kwantung Bureau, 150 judicial officers, 1,500
postal officers and employees of the Kwantung Bureau, 340 tax office officers
and employees, and 6,884 officers and employees of the Local Administration
Bureau of the South Manchuria Railway Company. The last figure included
an army of 2,663 teachers who were under the employment of the South
Manchuria Railway Company and who had passed into the employment of
the School Associations and Federation of School Associations.
Of the above mass transfer of personnel, the largest number naturally
came from the South Manchuria Railway Company. On November 30, 1937,
therefore, solemn ceremonies were held at Dairen and all other centers where
the S. M. R. Local Administration Offices are located to bid an official farewell
to the departing employees of the Company. And following this, the Local
Administration Bureau of the South Manchuria Railway Company, with its
thirty-year history of brilliant pioneership and achievement, had been dissolved.
The negotiations over various institutions which the South Manchuria Rail-
way Company has maintained for experimental purposes, which were to be
retained by the Company for the time being, had progressed smoothly after
the above great transfer and a perfect understanding was reached between the
South Manchuria Railway Company and the Manchoukuo Government by March,
1938. As a result, the second great transfer was made on April 1, 1938.
It involved the following institutions : (1) the Kungchuling Agricultural
Experimental Station ; (2) the Hsiungyaocheng Agricultural Experimental
Station ; (3) the Yamuingtzü Agricultural Experimental Station ; (4) the
Liaoyang Cotton Experimental Station ; (5) the Fenghuangcheng Tobacco
Experimental Station ; (6) the Taonan Agricultural Experimental Station ;
(7) the Linhsi Sheep Breeding Farm ; (8) the Kungchuling Sheep Breeding
Farm ; (9) the Veterinary Institute ; (10) the Geological Research Institute ;
(11) the Tumenling Forestry Experimental Station ; and (12) the Hsingcheng
Horticultural Experimental Station. With the above, the Health Research
Institute was transfered to the Kwantung Bureau and the Kwantung Army.
These institutions which served as the basis of various industrial activities
in the past were evaluated at 3,637,000 yen but were to be "loaned" to
the authorities mentioned without compensation for the time being. With
them, an additional number of 445 S. M. R. employees passed into the employ-
ment of Manchoukuo or the Kwantung Bureau.
Thus passed into history Japan's extraterritorial rights in Manchoukuo
and her administrative rights over the S. M. R. Zone. It is to the credit of
all parties concerned, their spirit of cooperation and careful preparations,
that such an epochal transition of first magnitude was consummated with
an amazing smoothness, even without a slightest hitch or difficulty. And
the satisfactory result of the procedure has strongly underwritten Japan's
trust placed upon Manchoukuo, as well as a phenomenal progress made in all
phases of Manchoukuo's statehood during its short span of six years.

大阪市

△市勢概観
大阪の地は往古難波と呼ばれる、海陸交通の要衝に位し神武天皇東征の際には征船をこの津に泊め給ふ、降つて仁徳天皇の高津宮御造営あり、隋唐との交通頻繁なるときには此地に鴻臚館を設けらる、その後豐公の築城成るに及んで商工業頓に興り近代大阪発展の端を開く、幾許もなくして冬夏兩陣の兵禍を被り市民は離散したが、松平忠明の治領するや鋭意復興につとめ市街を整理し、水路を開鑿し大阪再生の基礎を定む、徳川時代に入ってはその経済的発展はますます顯著で沈く海内の商権を握るに至り、また町人の都として文藝學術の方面にも異彩を放つた、明治二十二年市制實施により東西南北の四區を以て市域と定めたが、間もなく市域擴張の必要に迫られ明治三十年四月一日、隣接二十八ヶ町村を合併す、さらに日露戰爭及び世界大戰により市の經濟力著しく増大し、市街地の膨張もまた目覺しきものがあつたので、大正十四年四月一日には第二次擴張を行ひ、東成、西成の二郡四十四ヶ町村を編入し行政区畫を十三區に増した、かくて大阪市は今や人口二百五十萬を擁し、東洋第一の経済都市としての名實を具へるに至つた、また長らくも今上陛下には特に産業御視察の恩召で昭和四年六月四、五、六の三日間聖駕を大阪の地に駐めさせられ産業、教育その他の各種施設に臨幸を賜つたことは市史の上に永へに記念すべき光栄である。

THE 1931 FLOOD IN CHINA

TABLE 2
POPULATION AND CULTIVATED AREA OF 131 FLOODED HSIEN IN THE 1931 FLOOD AREA IN THE YANGTZE AND HWAI VALLEYS, CHINA.*

| Province | Number of flooded *hsien* in the province included in the study | Total farm families affected (00 omitted) | Per cent. of cultivated area flooded | Cultivated area (mow) flooded (00 omitted) | Total farm families (00 omitted) | Total cultivated area (mow) (00 omitted) |
| :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| Hunan | 15 | 4,242 | 51 | 89,634 | 9,088 | 174,059 |
| Hupeh | 30 | 10,227 | 55 | 139,183 | 19,919 | 253,427 |
| Kiangsi | 14 | 2,433 | 51 | 49,427 | 4,792 | 96,348 |
| South Anhwei | 24 | 6,132 | 62 | 86,797 | 9,906 | 140,227 |
| South Kiangsu | 11 | 2,243 | 43 | 40,255 | 5,375 | 93,675 |
| Honan | 1 | 636 | 85 | 31,875 | 748 | 37,500 |
| North Anhwei | 19 | 7,670 | 60 | 237,678 | 12,965 | 394,309 |
| North Kiangsu | 17 | 8,741 | 53 | 196,716 | 15,790 | 368,333 |
| Total | 131 | 42,324 | 56 | 871,565 | 78,583 | 1,557,878 |

*Most of the information on total farm families and total cultivated area per *hsien* is from data published under the direction of C. C. Chang of the former Statistical Bureau of the Legislative Yuan and from data collected in connection with the 1931 flood survey of The University of Nanking. Other sources were chiefly provincial government figures.

The percentages of cultivated area flooded are chiefly from estimates obtained from the 1931 flood survey of The University of Nanking and from planimetered data of land area flooded. Percentages from these two sources were checked with those obtained under the direction of C. C. Chang of the Directorate of Statistics and those reported by Magistrates to the National Flood Relief Commission, and with maps of area flooded.

For some *hsien* different sources gave great variation in the number of farm families and the amount of cultivated area. Determination of the more reasonable number was reached in part by computation of the density of population per square mile of cultivated area. Even the best figures give densities of great variation and often appear to be too high or too low. The average density of 1160 persons per square mile of cultivated area, for the entire area of the 131 *hsien* appears to be fairly reasonable as it checks with population densities previously obtained by the Department of Agricultural Economics, University of Nanking.

In cases of individual *hsien*, however, there may be serious underestimates of either number of families or of amount of cultivated area. For various reasons the amount of cultivated area is likely to be understated by at least 10-20 per cent.

tasks.output:
57

way Company to Manchoukuo from eleven cities and sixty-two towns and villages in the S. M. R. Zone alone were estimated at 31,438,994 yen and schools transfered to the Japanese authorities, 20,708,000 yen.

Together with this gigantic transfer, a total of nearly 14,000 persons, including Japanese and Manchurians, had passed into the employment of Manchoukuo, either directly or indirectly. Among them may be mentioned 1,396 police officers and men from the Japanese Embassy, 3,723 police officers and men from the Kwantung Bureau, 150 judicial officers, 1,500 postal officers and employees of the Kwantung Bureau, 340 tax office officers and employees, and 6,884 officers and employees of the Local Administration Bureau of the South Manchuria Railway Company. The last figure included an army of 2,663 teachers who were under the employment of the South Manchuria Railway Company and who had passed into the employment of the School Associations and Federation of School Associations.

Of the above mass transfer of personnel, the largest number naturally came from the South Manchuria Railway Company. On November 30, 1937, therefore, solemn ceremonies were held at Dairen and all other centers where the S. M. R. Local Administration Offices are located to bid an official farewell to the departing employees of the Company. And following this, the Local Administration Bureau of the South Manchuria Railway Company, with its thirty-year history of brilliant pioneership and achievement, had been dissolved.

The negotiations over various institutions which the South Manchuria Railway Company has maintained for experimental purposes, which were to be retained by the Company for the time being, had progressed smoothly after the above great transfer and a perfect understanding was reached between the South Manchuria Railway Company and the Manchoukuo Government by March, 1938. As a result, the second great transfer was made on April 1, 1938. It involved the following institutions: (1) the Kungchuling Agricultural Experimental Station; (2) the Hsiungyaocheng Agricultural Experimental Station; (3) the Yamuyingtsu Agricultural Experimental Station; (4) the Liaoyang Cotton Experimental Station; (5) the Fenghuangcheng Tobacco Experimental Station; (6) the Taonan Agricultural Experimental Station; (7) the Linhsi Sheep Breeding Farm; (8) the Kungchuling Sheep Breeding Farm; (9) the Veterinary Institute; (10) the Geological Research Institute; (11) the Tumenling Forestry Experimental Station; and (12) the Hsingcheng Horticultural Experimental Station. With the above, the Health Research Institute was transfered to the Kwantung Bureau and the Kwantung Army. These institutions which served as the basis of various industrial activities in the past were evaluated at 3,637,000 yen but were to be "loaned" to the authorities mentioned without compensation for the time being. With them, an additional number of 445 S. M. R. employees passed into the employment of Manchoukuo or the Kwantung Bureau.

Thus passed into history Japan's extraterritorial rights in Manchoukuo and her administrative rights over the S. M. R. Zone. It is to the credit of all parties concerned, their spirit of cooperation and careful preparations, that such an epochal transition of first magnitude was consummated with an amazing smoothness, even without a slightest hitch or difficulty. \*Most of the information on total farm families and total cultivated area per *hsien* is from data published under the direction of C. C. Chang of the former Statistical Bureau of the Legislative Yuan and from data collected in connection with the 1931 flood survey of The University of Nanking. Other sources were chiefly provincial government figures.
The percentages of cultivated area flooded are chiefly from estimates obtained from the 1931 flood survey of The University of Nanking and from planimetered data of land area flooded. Percentages from these two sources were checked with those obtained under the direction of C. C. Chang of the Directorate of Statistics and those reported by Magistrates to the National Flood Relief Commission, and with maps of area flooded.
For some *hsien* different sources gave great variation in the number of farm families and the amount of cultivated area. Determination of the more reasonable number was reached in part by computation of the density of population per square mile of cultivated area. Even the best figures give densities of great variation and often appear to be too high or too low. The average density of 1160 persons per square mile of cultivated area, for the entire area of the 131 *hsien* appears to be fairly reasonable as it checks with population densities previously obtained by the Department of Agricultural Economics, University of Nanking.
In cases of individual *hsien*, however, there may be serious underestimates of either number of families or of amount of cultivated area. For various reasons the amount of cultivated area is likely to be understated by at least 10-20 per cent.

tasks.output:
57

way Company to Manchoukuo from eleven cities and sixty-two towns and villages in the S. M. R. Zone alone were estimated at 31,438,994 yen and schools transfered to the Japanese authorities, 20,708,000 yen.

Together with this gigantic transfer, a total of nearly 14,000 persons, including Japanese and Manchurians, had passed into the employment of Manchoukuo, either directly or indirectly. Among them may be mentioned 1,396 police officers and men from the Japanese Embassy, 3,723 police officers and men from the Kwantung Bureau, 150 judicial officers, 1,500 postal officers and employees of the Kwantung Bureau, 340 tax office officers and employees, and 6,884 officers and employees of the Local Administration Bureau of the South Manchuria Railway Company. The last figure included an army of 2,663 teachers who were under the employment of the South Manchuria Railway Company and who had passed into the employment of the School Associations and Federation of School Associations.

Of the above mass transfer of personnel, the largest number naturally came from the South Manchuria Railway Company. On November 30, 1937, therefore, solemn ceremonies were held at Dairen and all other centers where the S. M. R. Local Administration Offices are located to bid an official farewell to the departing employees of the Company. And following this, the Local Administration Bureau of the South Manchuria Railway Company, with its thirty-year history of brilliant pioneering and achievement, had been dissolved.

The negotiations over various institutions which the South Manchuria Railway Company has maintained for experimental purposes, which were to be retained by the Company for the time being, had progressed smoothly after the above great transfer and a perfect understanding was reached between the South Manchuria Railway Company and the Manchoukuo Government by March, 1938. As a result, the second great transfer was made on April 1, 1938. It involved the following institutions: (1) the Kungchuling Agricultural Experimental Station; (2) the Hsiungyaocheng Agricultural Experimental Station; (3) the Yamuyingtzu Agricultural Experimental Station; (4) the Liaoyang Cotton Experimental Station; (5) the Fenghuangcheng Tobacco Experimental Station; (6) the Taonan Agricultural Experimental Station; (7) the Linhsi Sheep Breeding Farm; (8) the Kungchuling Sheep Breeding Farm; (9) the Veterinary Institute; (10) the Geological Research Institute; (11) the Tumenling Forestry Experimental Station; and (12) the Hsingcheng Horticultural Experimental Station. With the above, the Health Research Institute was transfered to the Kwantung Bureau and the Kwantung Army. These institutions which served as the basis of various industrial activities in the past were evaluated at 3,637,000 yen but were to be "loaned" to the authorities mentioned without compensation for the time being. With them, an additional number of 445 S. M. R. employees passed into the employment of Manchoukuo or the Kwantung Bureau.

Thus passed into history Japan's extraterritorial rights in Manchoukuo and her administrative rights over the S. M. R. Zone. It is to the credit of all parties concerned, their spirit of cooperation and careful preparations, that such an epochal transition of first magnitude was consummated with an amazing smoothness, even without a slightest hitch or difficulty. And the satisfactory result of the procedure has strongly underwritten Japan's trust placed upon Manchoukuo, as well as a phenomenal progress made in all phases of Manchoukuo's statehood during its short span of six years.

\*Most of the information on total farm families and total cultivated area per *hsien* is from data published under the direction of C. C. Chang of the former Statistical Bureau of the Legislative Yuan and from data collected in connection with the 1931 flood survey of The University of Nanking. Other sources were chiefly provincial government figures.

The percentages of cultivated area flooded are chiefly from estimates obtained from the 1931 flood survey of The University of Nanking and from planimetered data of land area flooded. Percentages from these two sources were checked with those obtained under the direction of C. C. Chang of the Directorate of Statistics and those reported by Magistrates to the National Flood Relief Commission, and with maps of area flooded.

For some *hsien* different sources gave great variation in the number of farm families and the amount of cultivated area. Determination of the more reasonable number was reached in part by computation of the density of population per square mile of cultivated area. Even the best figures give densities of great variation and often appear to be too high or too low. The average density of 1160 persons per square mile of cultivated area, for the entire area of the 131 *hsien* appears to be fairly reasonable as it checks with population densities previously obtained by the Department of Agricultural Economics, University of Nanking.

In cases of individual *hsien*, however, there may be serious underestimates of either number of families or of amount of cultivated area. For various reasons the amount of cultivated area is likely to be understated by at least 10-20 per cent.

tasks.output:
57

way Company to Manchoukuo from eleven cities and sixty-two towns and villages in the S. M. R. Zone alone were estimated at 31,438,994 yen and schools transfered to the Japanese authorities, 20,708,000 yen.

Together with this gigantic transfer, a total of nearly 14,000 persons, including Japanese and Manchurians, had passed into the employment of Manchoukuo, either directly or indirectly. Among them may be mentioned 1,396 police officers and men from the Japanese Embassy, 3,723 police officers and men from the Kwantung Bureau, 150 judicial officers, 1,500 postal officers and employees of the Kwantung Bureau, 340 tax office officers and employees, and 6,884 officers and employees of the Local Administration Bureau of the South Manchuria Railway Company. The last figure included an army of 2,663 teachers who were under the employment of the South Manchuria Railway Company and who had passed into the employment of the School Associations and Federation of School Associations.

Of the above mass transfer of personnel, the largest number naturally came from the South Manchuria Railway Company. On November 30, 1937, therefore, solemn ceremonies were held at Dairen and all other centers where the S. M. R. Local Administration Offices are located to bid an official farewell to the departing employees of the Company. And following this, the Local Administration Bureau of the South Manchuria Railway Company, with its thirty-year history of brilliant pioneership and achievement, had been dissolved.

The negotiations over various institutions which the South Manchuria Railway Company has maintained for experimental purposes, which were to be retained by the Company for the time being, had progressed smoothly after the above great transfer and a perfect understanding was reached between the South Manchuria Railway Company and the Manchoukuo Government by March, 1938. As a result, the second great transfer was made on April 1, 1938. It involved the following institutions: (1) the Kungchuling Agricultural Experimental Station; (2) the Hsiungyaocheng Agricultural Experimental Station; (3) the Yamuyingtzu Agricultural Experimental Station; (4) the Liaoyang Cotton Experimental Station; (5) the Fenghuangcheng Tobacco Experimental Station; (6) the Taonan Agricultural Experimental Station; (7) the Linhsi Sheep Breeding Farm; (8) the Kungchuling Sheep Breeding Farm; (9) the Veterinary Institute; (10) the Geological Research Institute; (11) the Tumenling Forestry Experimental Station; and (12) the Hsingcheng Horticultural Experimental Station. With the above, the Health Research Institute was transfered to the Kwantung Bureau and the Kwantung Army. These institutions which served as the basis of various industrial activities in the past were evaluated at 3,637,000 yen but were to be “loaned” to the authorities mentioned without compensation for the time being. With them, an additional number of 445 S. M. R. employees passed into the employment of Manchoukuo or the Kwantung Bureau.

Thus passed into history Japan’s extraterritorial rights in Manchoukuo and her administrative rights over the S. M. R. Zone. It is to the credit of all parties concerned, their spirit of cooperation and careful preparations, that such an epochal transition of first magnitude was consummated with an amazing smoothness, even without a slightest hitch or difficulty. And the satisfactory result of the procedure has strongly underwritten Japan’s trust placed upon Manchoukuo, as well as a phenomenal progress made in all phases of Manchoukuo’s statehood during its short span of six years.

大阪市

△市勢概觀

大阪の地は往古難波と呼ばる、海陸交通の要衝に位し神武天皇東征の際には征船をこの津に泊め給ふ、降つて仁德天皇の高津宮御造營あり、隋唐との交通頻繁なるときには此地に鴻臚館を設けらる、その後豐公の築城成るに及んで商工業頓に興り近代大阪發展の端を開く、幾許もなくして冬夏兩陣の兵禍を被り市民は離散したが、松平忠明の治領するや銳意復興につとめ市街を整理し、水路を開鑿し大阪再生の基礎を定む、德川時代に入つてはその經濟的發展はます／＼顯著で汎く海內の商權を握るに至り、また町人の都として文藝學術の方面にも異彩を放つた、明治22年市制實施により東西南北の4區を以て市域と定めたが、間もなく市域擴張の必要に迫られ明治30年4月1日、隣接28ケ町村を合併す、さらに日露戰爭及び世界大戰により市の經濟力著しく增大し、市街地の膨脹もまた目覺しきものがあつたので、大正14年4月1日には第2次擴張を行ひ、東成、西成の2郡44ケ町村を編入し行政區劃を13區に增した、かくて大阪市は今や人口250萬を擁し、東洋第1の經濟都市としての名實を具へるに至つた、また畏くも今上陛下には特に產業御奬勵の思召で昭和4年6月4、5、6の3日間聖駕を大阪の地に駐めさせられ產業、敎育その他の各種施設に臨幸を賜つたことは市史の上に永へに記念すべき光榮である。

Percentages from these two sources were checked with those obtained under the direction of C. C. Chang of the Directorate of Statistics and those reported by Magistrates to the National Flood Relief Commission, and with maps of area flooded.

For some hsien different sources gave great variation in the number of farm families and the amount of cultivated area. Determination of the more reasonable number was reached in part by computation of the density of population per square mile of cultivated area. Even the best figures give densities of great variation and often appear to be too high or too low. The average density of 1160 persons per square mile of cultivated area, for the entire area of the 131 hsien appears to be fairly reasonable as it checks with population densities previously obtained by the Department of Agricultural Economics, University of Nanking.

In cases of individual hsien, however, there may be serious underestimates of either number of families or of amount of cultivated area. For various reasons the amount of cultivated area is likely to be understated by at least 10-20 per cent.

57

way Company to Manchoukuo from eleven cities and sixty-two towns and villages in the S. M. R. Zone alone were estimated at 31,438,994 yen and schools transferred to the Japanese authorities, 20,708,000 yen.

Together with this gigantic transfer, a total of nearly 14,000 persons, including Japanese and Manchurians, had passed into the employment of Manchoukuo, either directly or indirectly. Among them may be mentioned 1,396 police officers and men from the Japanese Embassy, 3,723 police officers and men from the Kwantung Bureau, 150 judicial officers, 1,500 postal officers and employees of the Kwantung Bureau, 340 tax office officers and employees, and 6,884 officers and employees of the Local Administration Bureau of the South Manchuria Railway Company. The last figure included an army of 2,663 teachers who were under the employment of the South Manchuria Railway Company and who had passed into the employment of the School Associations and Federation of School Associations.

Of the above mass transfer of personnel, the largest number naturally came from the South Manchuria Railway Company. On November 30, 1937, therefore, solemn ceremonies were held at Dairen and all other centers where the S. M. R. Local Administration Offices are located to bid an official farewell to the departing employees of the Company. And following this, the Local Administration Bureau of the South Manchuria Railway Company, with its thirty-year history of brilliant pioneership and achievement, had been dissolved.

The negotiations over various institutions which the South Manchuria Railway Company has maintained for experimental purposes, which were to be retained by the Company for the time being, had progressed smoothly after the above great transfer and a perfect understanding was reached between the South Manchuria Railway Company and the Manchoukuo Government by March, 1938. As a result, the second great transfer was made on April 1, 1938. It involved the following institutions: (1) the Kungchuling Agricultural Experimental Station; (2) the Hsiungyaocheng Agricultural Experimental Station; (3) the Yamuyingtzu Agricultural Experimental Station; (4) the Liaoyang Cotton Experimental Station; (5) the Fenghuangcheng Tobacco Experimental Station; (6) the Taonan Agricultural Experimental Station; (7) the Linhsi Sheep Breeding Farm; (8) the Kungchuling Sheep Breeding Farm; (9) the Veterinary Institute; (10) the Geological Research Institute; (11) the Tumenling Forestry Experimental Station; and (12) the Hsingcheng Horticultural Experimental Station. With the above, the Health Research Institute was transferred to the Kwantung Bureau and the Kwantung Army. These institutions which served as the basis of various industrial activities in the past were evaluated at 3,637,000 yen but were to be “loaned” to the authorities mentioned without compensation for the time being. With them, an additional number of 445 S. M. R. employees passed into the employment of Manchoukuo or the Kwantung Bureau.

Thus passed into history Japan’s extraterritorial rights in Manchoukuo and her administrative rights over the S. M. R. Zone. It is to the credit of all parties concerned, their spirit of cooperation and careful preparations, that such an epochal transition of first magnitude was consummated with an amazing smoothness, even without a slightest hitch or difficulty. And the satisfactory result of the procedure has strongly underwritten Japan’s trust placed upon Manchoukuo, as well as a phenomenal progress made in all phases of Manchoukuo’s statehood during its short span of six years.

大阪の地は往古難波と呼ばる、海陸交通の要衝に位し神武天皇東征の際には征船をこの津に泊め給ふ、降って仁徳天皇の高津宮御造営あり、階層との交通頻繁なるときには此地に鴻臚館を設けらる、その後豊公の築城成るに及んで商工業頓に興り近代大阪発展の端を開く、幾許もなくして冬夏両陣の兵禍を被り市民は離散したが、松平忠明の治領するや鋭意復興につとめ市街を整理し水路を開鑿し大阪再生の基礎を定む、徳川時代に入ってはその経済的発展はますます顕著で弘く海内の商権を握るに至り、また町人の都として文藝學術の方面にも異彩を放った、明治21年市制実施により東西南北の四區を以て市域と定めたが、間もなく市域擴張の必要に迫られ明治30年4月1日、隣接28ヶ町村を合併し、さらに日露戰争及び世界大戰により市の経済力著しく増大し、市街地の膨脹もまた目覺しきものがあったので、大正14年4月1日には第二次擴張を行ひ、東成、西成の2郡44ヶ町村を編入し行政區劃を13區に増した、かくて大阪市は今や人口253萬を擁し、東洋第一の經濟都市としての名實を具へるに至った、また畏くも今上陛下には昭和4年6月4日、5、6の3日間聖駕を大阪の地に駐めさせられ、産業、敎育その他の各種施設に臨幸を賜つたことは市史の上に永へに記念すべき光榮である

*Most of the information on total farm families and total cultivated area per *hsien* is from data published under the direction of C. C. Chang of the former Statistical Bureau of the Legislative Yuan and from data collected in connection with the 1931 flood survey of The University of Nanking. Other sources were chiefly provincial government figures.

The percentages of cultivated area flooded are chiefly from estimates obtained from the 1931 flood survey of The University of Nanking and from planimetered data of land area flooded. Percentages from these two sources were checked with those obtained under the direction of C. C. Chang of the Directorate of Statistics and those reported by Magistrates to the National Flood Relief Commission, and with maps of area flooded.

For some *hsien* different sources gave great variation in the number of farm families and the amount of cultivated area. Determination of the more reasonable number was reached in part by computation of the density of population per square mile of cultivated area. Even the best figures give densities of great variation and often appear to be too high or too low. The average density of 1160 persons per square mile of cultivated area, for the entire area of the 131 *hsien* appears to be fairly reasonable as it checks with population densities previously obtained by the Department of Agricultural Economics, University of Nanking.

In cases of individual *hsien*, however, there may be serious underestimates of either number of families or of amount of cultivated area. For various reasons the amount of cultivated area is likely to be understated by at least 10-20 per cent.

tasks.output:
way Company to Manchoukuo from eleven cities and sixty-two towns and villages in the S. M. R. Zone alone were estimated at 31,438,994 yen and schools transferred to the Japanese authorities, 20,708,000 yen.

Together with this gigantic transfer, a total of nearly 14,000 persons, including Japanese and Manchurians, had passed into the employment of Manchoukuo, either directly or indirectly. Among them may be mentioned 1,396 police officers and men from the Japanese Embassy, 3,723 police officers and men from the Kwantung Bureau, 150 judicial officers, 1,500 postal officers and employees of the Kwantung Bureau, 340 tax office officers and employees, and 6,884 officers and employees of the Local Administration Bureau of the South Manchuria Railway Company. The last figure included an army of 2,663 teachers who were under the employment of the South Manchuria Railway Company and who had passed into the employment of the School Associations and Federation of School Associations.

Of the above mass transfer of personnel, the largest number naturally came from the South Manchuria Railway Company. On November 30, 1937, therefore, solemn ceremonies were held at Dairen and all other centers where the S. M. R. Local Administration Offices are located to bid an official farewell to the departing employees of the Company. And following this, the Local Administration Bureau of the South Manchuria Railway Company, with its thirty-year history of brilliant pioneership and achievement, had been dissolved.

The negotiations over various institutions which the South Manchuria Railway Company has maintained for experimental purposes, which were to be retained by the Company for the time being, had progressed smoothly after the above great transfer and a perfect understanding was reached between the South Manchuria Railway Company and the Manchoukuo Government by March, 1938. As a result, the second great transfer was made on April 1, 1938. It involved the following institutions: (1) the Kungchuling Agricultural Experimental Station; (2) the Hsiungyaocheng Agricultural Experimental Station; (3) the Yamuyingtzu Agricultural Experimental Station; (4) the Liaoyang Cotton Experimental Station; (5) the Fenghuangcheng Tobacco Experimental Station; (6) the Taonan Agricultural Experimental Station; (7) the Linhsi Sheep Breeding Farm; (8) the Kungchuling Sheep Breeding Farm; (9) the Veterinary Institute; (10) the Geological Research Institute; (11) the Tumenling Forestry Experimental Station; and (12) the Hsingcheng Horticultural Experimental Station. With the above, the Health Research Institute was transferred to the Kwantung Bureau and the Kwantung Army. These institutions which served as the basis of various industrial activities in the past were evaluated at 3,637,000 yen but were to be “loaned” to the authorities mentioned without compensation for the time being. With them, an additional number of 445 S. M. R. employees passed into the employment of Manchoukuo or the Kwantung Bureau.

Thus passed into history Japan’s extraterritorial rights in Manchoukuo and her administrative rights over the S. M. R. Zone. It is to the credit of all parties concerned, their spirit of cooperation and careful preparations, that such an epochal transition of first magnitude was consummated with an amazing smoothness, even without a slightest hitch or difficulty. And the satisfactory result of the procedure has strongly underwritten Japan’s trust placed upon Manchoukuo, as well as a phenomenal progress made in all phases of Manchoukuo’s statehood during its short span of six years.

市阪大

大阪市

△市勢概觀

大阪の地は往古難波と呼ばれ、海陸交通の要衝に位し神武天皇東征の際には征船をこの津に泊め給ふ、降って仁徳天皇の高津宮御造營あり、階層との交潤繁栄なるときには此地に鴻臚館を設けらる、その後豊公の築城成るに及んで商工業頓に興り近代大阪發展の端を開く、幾許もなくして冬夏兩陣の兵禍を被り市民は離散したが、松平忠明の治領するや鋭意復興につとめ市街を整理し水路を開鑿し大阪再生の基礎を定む、徳川時代に入つてはその經濟的發展はますます顯著で犯く海内の商權を握るに至り、また町人の都として文藝學術の方面にも異彩を放つた、明治22年市制實施により東西南北の4區を以て市域と定めたが、間もなく市域擴張の必要に迫られ明治30年4月1日、隣接28ケ町村を合併す、さらに日露戰爭及び世界大戰により市の經濟力著しく増大し、市街地の膨脹もまた目覺しきものがあつたので、大正14年4月1日には第二次擴張を行ひ、東成、西成の2郡44ケ町村を編入し行政區劃を13區に增した、かくて大阪市は今や人口255萬を擁し、東洋第一の經濟都市としての名聲を

具へるに至つた、また畏くも今上陛下には特に産業御視察の思召で昭和4年6月4、5、6の3日間聖駕を大阪の地に駐めさせられ産業、教育その他の各種施設に臨幸を賜つたことは市史の上に永へに記念すべき光榮である。

THE 1931 FLOOD IN CHINA

TABLE 2

POPULATION AND CULTIVATED AREA OF 131 FLOODED HSIEN  
IN THE 1931 FLOOD AREA IN THE YANGTZE  
AND HWAI VALLEYS, CHINA.*

| Province | Number of flooded hsien in the province included in the study | Total farm families affected (00 omitted) | Per cent. of cultivated area flooded | Cultivated area (mow) flooded (00 omitted) | Total farm families (00 omitted) | Total cultivated area (mow) (00 omitted) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Hunan | 15 | 4,242 | 51 | 89,634 | 9,088 | 174,059 |
| Hupeh | 30 | 10,227 | 55 | 139,183 | 19,919 | 253,427 |
| Kiangsi | 14 | 2,433 | 51 | 49,427 | 4,792 | 96,348 |
| South Anhwei | 24 | 6,132 | 62 | 86,797 | 9,906 | 140,227 |
| South Kiangsu | 11 | 2,243 | 43 | 40,255 | 5,375 | 93,675 |
| Honan | 1 | 636 | 85 | 31,875 | 748 | 37,500 |
| North Anhwei | 19 | 7,670 | 60 | 237,678 | 12,965 | 394,309 |
| North Kiangsu | 17 | 8,741 | 53 | 196,716 | 15,790 | 368,333 |
| Total | 131 | 42,324 | 56 | 871,565 | 78,583 | 1,557,878 |

*Most of the information on total farm families and total cultivated area per hsien is from data published under the direction of C. C. Chang of the former Statistical Bureau of the Legislative Yuan and from data collected in connection with the 1931 flood survey of The University of Nanking. Other sources were chiefly provincial government figures.

The percentages of cultivated area flooded are chiefly from estimates obtained from the 1931 flood survey of The University of Nanking and from planimetered data of land area flooded. Percentages from these two sources were checked with those obtained under the direction of C. C. Chang of the Directorate of Statistics and those reported by Magistrates to the National Flood Relief Commission, and with maps of area flooded.

For some hsien different sources gave great variation in the number of farm families and the amount of cultivated area. Determination of the more reasonable number was reached in part by computation of the density of population per square mile of cultivated area. Even the best figures give densities of great variation and often appear to be too high or too low. The average density of 1160 persons per square mile of cultivated area, for the entire area of the 131 hsien appears to be fairly reasonable as it checks with population densities previously obtained by the Department of Agricultural Economics, University of Nanking.

In cases of individual hsien, however, there may be serious underestimates of either number of families or of amount of cultivated area. For various reasons the amount of cultivated area is likely to be understated by at least 10-20 per cent.

57

way Company to Manchoukuo from eleven cities and sixty-two towns and villages in the S. M. R. Zone alone were estimated at 31,438,994 yen and schools transferred to the Japanese authorities, 20,708,000 yen.

Together with this gigantic transfer, a total of nearly 14,000 persons, including Japanese and Manchurians, had passed into the employment of Manchoukuo, either directly or indirectly. Among them may be mentioned 1,396 police officers and men from the Japanese Embassy, 3,723 police officers and men from the Kwantung Bureau, 150 judicial officers, 1,500 postal officers and employees of the Kwantung Bureau, 340 tax office officers and employees, and 6,884 officers and employees of the Local Administration Bureau of the South Manchuria Railway Company. The last figure included an army of 2,663 teachers who were under the employment of the South Manchuria Railway Company and who had passed into the employment of the School Associations and Federation of School Associations.

Of the above mass transfer of personnel, the largest number naturally came from the South Manchuria Railway Company. On November 30, 1937, therefore, solemn ceremonies were held at Dairen and all other centers where the S. M. R. Local Administration Offices are located to bid an official farewell to the departing employees of the Company. And following this, the Local Administration Bureau of the South Manchuria Railway Company, with its thirty-year history of brilliant pioneership and achievement, had been dissolved.

The negotiations over various institutions which the South Manchuria Railway Company has maintained for experimental purposes, which were to be retained by the Company for the time being, had progressed smoothly after the above great transfer and a perfect understanding was reached between the South Manchuria Railway Company and the Manchoukuo Government by March, 1938. As a result, the second great transfer was made on April 1, 1938. It involved the following institutions: (1) the Kungchuling Agricultural Experimental Station; (2) the Hsiungyaocheng Agricultural Experimental Station; (3) the Yamuyingtzu Agricultural Experimental Station; (4) the Liaoyang Cotton Experimental Station; (5) the Fenghuangcheng Tobacco Experimental Station; (6) the Taonan Agricultural Experimental Station; (7) the Linhsi Sheep Breeding Farm; (8) the Kungchuling Sheep Breeding Farm; (9) the Veterinary Institute; (10) the Geological Research Institute; (11) the Tumenling Forestry Experimental Station; and (12) the Hsingcheng Horticultural Experimental Station. With the above, the Health Research Institute was transferred to the Kwantung Bureau and the Kwantung Army. These institutions which served as the basis of various industrial activities in the past were evaluated at 3,637,000 yen but were to be “loaned” to the authorities mentioned without compensation for the time being. With them, an additional number of 445 S. M. R. employees passed into the employment of Manchoukuo or the Kwantung Bureau.

Thus passed into history Japan’s extraterritorial rights in Manchoukuo and her administrative rights over the S. M. R. Zone. It is to the credit of all parties concerned, their spirit of cooperation and careful preparations, that such an epochal transition of first magnitude was consummated with an amazing smoothness, even without a slightest hitch or difficulty. And the satisfactory result of the procedure has strongly underwritten Japan’s trust placed upon Manchoukuo, as well as a phenomenal progress made in all phases of Manchoukuo’s statehood during its short span of six years.

大阪の地は往古難波と呼ばる、海陸交通の要衝に位し神武天皇東征の際には征船をこの津に泊め給ふ、降って仁徳天皇の高津宮御造営あり、隣居との交通頻繁なるときには此地に鴻臚館を設けらる、その後豊公の築城成るに及んで商工業頓に興り近代大阪發展の端を開く、幾許もなくして冬夏両陣の兵燹を被り市民は離散したが、松平忠明の治領するや鋭意復興につとめ市街を整理し水路を開鑿し大阪再生の基礎を定む、徳川時代に入ってはその経済的發展はますます顕著で凡く海内の商権を握るに至り、また町人の都として文藝學術の方面にも異彩を放った、明治21年市制實施により東西南北の4區を以て市域と定めたが、間もなく市域擴張の必要に迫られ明治30年4月1日、隣接28ヶ町村を合併、さらに日露戰爭及び世界大戰により市の經濟力著しく増大し、市街地の膨脹もまた目覺しきものがあったので、大正14年4月1日には第二次擴張を行ひ、東成、西成の2郡44ヶ町村を編入し行政區劃を13區に増した。かくて大阪市は今や人口250萬を擁し、東洋第一の經濟都市としての名實を具へるに至った。また畏くも今上陛下には昭和4年6月4、5、6の3日間聖駕を大阪の地に駐めさせられ産業、教育その他の各種施設に臨幸を賜ったことは市史の上に永へに記念すべき光栄である。

*Most of the information on total farm families and total cultivated area per hsien is from data published under the direction of C. C. Other sources were chiefly provincial government figures.

The percentages of cultivated area flooded are chiefly from estimates obtained from the 1931 flood survey of The University of Nanking and from planimetered data of land area flooded. Percentages from these two sources were checked with those obtained under the direction of C. C. Chang of the Directorate of Statistics and those reported by Magistrates to the National Flood Relief Commission, and with maps of area flooded.

For some hsien different sources gave great variation in the number of farm families and the amount of cultivated area. Determination of the more reasonable number was reached in part by computation of the density of population per square mile of cultivated area. Even the best figures give densities of great variation and often appear to be too high or too low. The average density of 1160 persons per square mile of cultivated area, for the entire area of the 131 hsien appears to be fairly reasonable as it checks with population densities previously obtained by the Department of Agricultural Economics, University of Nanking.

In cases of individual hsien, however, there may be serious underestimates of either number of families or of amount of cultivated area. For various reasons the amount of cultivated area is likely to be understated by at least 10-20 per cent.

57

way Company to Manchoukuo from eleven cities and sixty-two towns and villages in the S. M. R. Zone alone were estimated at 31,438,994 yen and schools transferred to the Japanese authorities, 20,708,000 yen.

Together with this gigantic transfer, a total of nearly 14,000 persons, including Japanese and Manchurians, had passed into the employment of Manchoukuo, either directly or indirectly. Among them may be mentioned 1,396 police officers and men from the Japanese Embassy, 3,723 police officers and men from the Kwantung Bureau, 150 judicial officers, 1,500 postal officers and employees of the Kwantung Bureau, 340 tax office officers and employees, and 6,884 officers and employees of the Local Administration Bureau of the South Manchuria Railway Company. The last figure included an army of 2,663 teachers who were under the employment of the South Manchuria Railway Company and who had passed into the employment of the School Associations and Federation of School Associations.

Of the above mass transfer of personnel, the largest number naturally came from the South Manchuria Railway Company. On November 30, 1937, therefore, solemn ceremonies were held at Dairen and all other centers where the S. M. R. Local Administration Offices are located to bid an official farewell to the departing employees of the Company. And following this, the Local Administration Bureau of the South Manchuria Railway Company, with its thirty-year history of brilliant pioneership and achievement, had been dissolved.

TABLE 2
POPULATION AND CULTIVATED AREA OF 131 FLOODED HSIEN
IN THE 1931 FLOOD AREA IN THE YANGTZE
AND HWAI VALLEYS, CHINA.*

| Province | Number of flooded hsien in the province included in the study | Total farm families affected (00 omitted) | Per cent. of cultivated area flooded | Cultivated area (mow) flooded (00 omitted) | Total farm families (00 omitted) | Total cultivated area (mow) (00 omitted) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Hunan | 15 | 4,242 | 51 | 89,634 | 9,088 | 174,059 |
| Hupeh | 30 | 10,227 | 55 | 139,183 | 19,919 | 253,427 |
| Kiangsi | 14 | 2,433 | 51 | 49,427 | 4,792 | 96,348 |
| South Anhwei | 24 | 6,132 | 62 | 86,797 | 9,906 | 140,227 |
| South Kiangsu | 11 | 2,243 | 43 | 40,255 | 5,375 | 93,675 |
| Honan | 1 | 636 | 85 | 31,875 | 748 | 37,500 |
| North Anhwei | 19 | 7,670 | 60 | 237,678 | 12,965 | 394,309 |
| North Kiangsu | 17 | 8,741 | 53 | 196,716 | 15,790 | 368,333 |
| Total | 131 | 42,324 | 56 | 871,565 | 78,583 | 1,557,878 |

*Most of the information on total farm families and total cultivated area per hsien is from data published under the direction of C. C. Chang of the former Statistical Bureau of the Legislative Yuan and from data collected in connection with the 1931 flood survey of The University of Nanking. Other sources were chiefly provincial government figures.
The percentages of cultivated area flooded are chiefly from estimates obtained from the 1931 flood survey of The University of Nanking and from planimetered data of land area flooded. Percentages from these two sources were checked with those obtained under the direction of C. C. Chang of the Directorate of Statistics and those reported by Magistrates to the National Flood Relief Commission, and with maps of area flooded.
For some hsien different sources gave great variation in the number of farm families and the amount of cultivated area. Determination of the more reasonable number was reached in part by computation of the density of population per square mile of cultivated area. Even the best figures give densities of great variation and often appear to be too high or too low. The average density of 1,160 persons per square mile of cultivated area, for the entire area of the 131 hsien appears to be fairly reasonable as it checks with population densities previously obtained by the Department of Agricultural Economics, University of Nanking.
In cases of individual hsien, however, there may be serious underestimates of either number of families or of amount of cultivated area. For various reasons the amount of cultivated area is likely to be understated by at least 10-20 per cent.

大阪の地は往古難波とよぶ、海陸交通の要衝に位し神武天皇東征の際には征船をこの津に泊め給ふ、降つて仁徳天皇の高津宮御造営あり、隋唐との交通頻繁なるときには此地に鴻臚館を設ける、その後豐公の築城成るに及んで商工業に興り近代大阪發展の端を開く、幾許もなくして冬夏兩陣の兵禍を被り市民は離散したが、松平忠明の治領するや銳意復興に努め市街を整理し、水路を開鑿し大坂再生の基礎を定む、徳川時代に入つてはその經濟的發展はますます顯著で汎く海内の商權を握るに至り、また町人の都として文藝學術の方面にも異彩を放つた、明治22年市制實施により東西南北の4區を以て市域と定めたが、間もなく市域擴張の必要に迫れ併す、さらに日露戰爭及び世界大戰により市の經濟力著しく增大し、市街地の膨脹もまた目覺しきものがあつたので、大正14年4月1日には第2次擴張を行ひ、東成、西成の2郡44ケ町村を編入し行政區割を13區に増した、かくて大阪市は今や人口250萬を擁し、東洋第一の經濟都市としての名實を具へるに至つた、また畏くも今上陛下には特に産業御視察の思召で昭和4年6月4、5、6の3日間聖駕を大阪の地に駐めさせられ産業、教育その他の各種施設に臨幸を賜つたことは市史の上に永へに記憶すべき光榮である。

57

way Company to Manchoukuo from eleven cities and sixty-two towns and villages in the S. M. R. Zone alone were estimated at 31,438,994 yen and schools transfered to the Japanese authorities, 20,708,000 yen.

Together with this gigantic transfer, a total of nearly 14,000 persons, including Japanese and Manchurians, had passed into the employment of Manchoukuo, either directly or indirectly. Among them may be mentioned 1,396 police officers and men from the Japanese Embassy, 3,723 police officers and men from the Kwantung Bureau, 150 judicial officers, 1,500 postal officers and employees of the Kwantung Bureau, 340 tax office officers and employees, and 6,884 officers and employees of the Local Administration Bureau of the South Manchuria Railway Company. The last figure included an army of 2,663 teachers who were under the employment of the South Manchuria Railway Company and who had passed into the employment of the School Associations and Federation of School Associations.

Of the above mass transfer of personnel, the largest number naturally came from the South Manchuria Railway Company. On November 30, 1937, therefore, solemn ceremonies were held at Dairen and all other centers where the S. M. R. Local Administration Offices are located to bid an official farewell to the departing employees of the Company. And following this, the Local Administration Bureau of the South Manchuria Railway Company, with its thirty-year history of brilliant pioneership and achievement, had been dissolved.

The negotiations over various institutions which the South Manchuria Railway Company has maintained for experimental purposes, which were to be retained by the Company for the time being, had progressed smoothly after the above great transfer and a perfect understanding was reached between the South Manchuria Railway Company and the Manchoukuo Government by March, 1938. As a result, the second great transfer was made on April 1, 1938. It involved the following institutions: (1) the Kungchuling Agricultural Experimental Station; (2) the Hsiungyaocheng Agricultural Experimental Station; (3) the Yamuyingtsu Agricultural Experimental Station; (4) the Liaoyang Cotton Experimental Station; (5) the Fenghuangcheng Tobacco Experimental Station; (6) the Taonan Agricultural Experimental Station; (7) the Linhsi Sheep Breeding Farm; (8) the Kungchuling Sheep Breeding Farm; (9) the Veterinary Institute; (10) the Geological Research Institute; (11) the Tumenling Forestry Experimental Station; and (12) the Hsingcheng Horticultural Experimental Station. With the above, the Health Research Institute was transfered to the Kwantung Bureau and the Kwantung Army. These institutions which served as the basis of various industrial activities in the past were evaluated at 3,637,000 yen but were to be "loaned" to the authorities mentioned without compensation for the time being. With them, an additional number of 445 S. M. R. employees passed into the employ-ment of Manchoukuo or the Kwantung Bureau.

Thus passed into history Japan's extraterritorial rights in Manchoukuo and her administrative rights over the S. M. R. Zone. It is to the credit of all parties concerned, their spirit of cooperation and careful preparations, that such an epochal transition of first magnitude was consummated with an amazing smoothness, even without a slightest hitch or difficulty. And the satisfactory result of the procedure has strongly underwritten Japan's trust placed upon Manchoukuo, as well as a phenomenal progress made in all phases of Manchoukuo's statehood during its short span of six years.

| :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |

| Total | 131 | 42,324 | 56 | 871,565 | 78,583 | 1,557,878 |

*Most of the information on total farm families and total cultivated area per *hsien* is from data published under the direction of C. C. Chang of the former Statistical Bureau of the Legislative Yuan and from data collected in connection with the 1931 flood survey of The University of Nanking. Other sources were chiefly provincial government figures.
The percentages of cultivated area flooded are chiefly from estimates obtained from the 1931 flood survey of The University of Nanking and from planimetered data of land area flooded. Percentages from these two sources were checked with those obtained under the direction of C. C. Chang of the Directorate of Statistics and those reported by Magistrates to the National Flood Relief Commission, and with maps of area flooded.
For some *hsien* different sources gave great variation in the number of farm families and the amount of cultivated area. Determination of the more reasonable number was reached in part by computation of the density of population per square mile of cultivated area. Even the best figures give densities of great variation and often appear to be too high or too low. The average density of 1160 persons per square mile of cultivated area, for the entire area of the 131 *hsien* appears to be fairly reasonable as it checks with population densities previously obtained by the Department of Agricultural Economics, University of Nanking.
In cases of individual *hsien*, however, there may be serious underestimates of either number of families or of amount of cultivated area. For various reasons the amount of cultivated area is likely to be understated by at least 10-20 per cent.

57
way Company to Manchoukuo from eleven cities and sixty-two towns and villages in the S. M. R. Zone alone were estimated at 31,438,994 yen and schools transfered to the Japanese authorities, 20,708,000 yen.
Together with this gigantic transfer, a total of nearly 14,000 persons, including Japanese and Manchurians, had passed into the employment of Manchoukuo, either directly or indirectly. Among them may be mentioned 1,396 police officers and men from the Japanese Embassy, 3,723 police officers and men from the Kwantung Bureau, 150 judicial officers, 1,500 postal officers and employees of the Kwantung Bureau, 340 tax office officers and employees, and 6,884 officers and employees of the Local Administration Bureau of the South Manchuria Railway Company. The last figure included an army of 2,663 teachers who were under the employment of the South Manchuria Railway Company and who had passed into the employment of the School Associations and Federation of School Associations.
Of the above mass transfer of personnel, the largest number naturally came from the South Manchuria Railway Company. On November 30, 1937, therefore, solemn ceremonies were held at Dairen and all other centers where the S. M. R. Local Administration Offices are located to bid an official farewell to the departing employees of the Company. And following this, the Local Administration Bureau of the South Manchuria Railway Company, with its thirty-year history of brilliant pioneership and achievement, had been dissolved.
The negotiations over various institutions which the South Manchuria Railway Company has maintained for experimental purposes, which were to be retained by the Company for the time being, had progressed smoothly after the above great transfer and a perfect understanding was reached between the South Manchuria Railway Company and the Manchoukuo Government by March, 1938. As a result, the second great transfer was made on April 1, 1938. It involved the following institutions: (1) the Kungchuling Agricultural Experimental Station; (2) the Hsiungyaocheng Agricultural Experimental Station; (3) the Yamuyingtzu Agricultural Experimental Station; (4) the Liaoyang Cotton Experimental Station; (5) the Fenghuangcheng Tobacco Experimental Station; (6) the Taonan Agricultural Experimental Station; (7) the Linhsi Sheep Breeding Farm; (8) the Kungchuling Sheep Breeding Farm; (9) the Veterinary Institute; (10) the Geological Research Institute; (11) the Tumenling Forestry Experimental Station; and (12) the Hsingcheng Horticultural Experimental Station. With the above, the Health Research Institute was transfered to the Kwantung Bureau and the Kwantung Army. These institutions which served as the basis of various industrial activities in the past were evaluated at 3,637,000 yen but were to be "loaned" to the authorities mentioned without compensation for the time being. With them, an additional number of 445 S. M. R. employees passed into the employment of Manchoukuo or the Kwantung Bureau.
Thus passed into history Japan's extraterritorial rights in Manchoukuo and her administrative rights over the S. M. R. Zone. It is to the credit of all parties concerned, their spirit of cooperation and careful preparations, that such an epochal transition of first magnitude was consummated with an amazing smoothness, even without a slightest hitch or difficulty. And the satisfactory result of the procedure has strongly underwritten Japan's trust placed upon Manchoukuo, as well as a phenomenal progress made in all phases of Manchoukuo's statehood during its short span of six years.

THE 1931 FLOOD IN CHINA
TABLE 2
POPULATION AND CULTIVATED AREA OF 131 FLOODED HSIEN
IN THE 1931 FLOOD AREA IN THE YANGTZE
AND HWAI VALLEYS, CHINA.*

| Province | Number of flooded hsien in the province included in the study | Total farm families affected (00 omitted) | Per cent. of cultivated area flooded | Cultivated area (mow) flooded (00 omitted) | Total farm families (00 omitted) | Total cultivated area (mow) (00 omitted) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Hunan | 15 | 4,242 | 51 | 89,634 | 9,088 | 174,059 |
| Hupeh | 30 | 10,227 | 55 | 139,183 | 19,919 | 253,427 |
| Kiangsi | 14 | 2,433 | 51 | 49,427 | 4,792 | 96,348 |
| South Anhwei | 24 | 6,132 | 62 | 86,797 | 9,906 | 140,227 |
| South Kiangsu | 11 | 2,243 | 43 | 40,255 | 5,375 | 93,675 |
| Honan | 1 | 636 | 85 | 31,875 | 748 | 37,500 |
| North Anhwei | 19 | 7,670 | 60 | 237,678 | 12,965 | 394,309 |
| North Kiangsu | 17 | 8,741 | 53 | 196,716 | 15,790 | 368,333 |
| Total | 131 | 42,324 | 56 | 871,565 | 78,583 | 1,557,878 |

*Most of the information on total farm families and total cultivated area per hsien is from data published under the direction of C. C. Chang of the former Statistical Bureau of the Legislative Yuan and from data collected in connection with the 1931 flood survey of The University of Nanking. Other sources were chiefly provincial government figures.
The percentages of cultivated area flooded are chiefly from estimates obtained from the 1931 flood survey of The University of Nanking and from planimetered data of land area flooded. Percentages from these two sources were checked with those obtained under the direction of C. C. Chang of the Directorate of Statistics and those reported by Magistrates to the National Flood Relief Commission, and with maps of area flooded.
For some hsien different sources gave great variation in the number of farm families and the amount of cultivated area. Determination of the more reasonable number was reached in part by computation of the density of population per square mile of cultivated area. Even the best figures give densities of great variation and often appear to be too high or too low. The average density of 1160 persons per square mile of cultivated area, for the entire area of the 131 hsien appears to be fairly reasonable as it checks with population densities previously obtained by the Department of Agricultural Economics, University of Nanking.
In cases of individual hsien, however, there may be serious underestimates of either number of families or of amount of cultivated area. For various reasons the amount of cultivated area is likely to be understated by at least 10-20 per cent.

tasks.output:
way Company to Manchoukuo from eleven cities and sixty-two towns and villages in the S.M.R. Zone alone were estimated at 31,438,994 yen and schools transferred to the Japanese authorities, 20,708,000 yen.

Together with this gigantic transfer, a total of nearly 14,000 persons, including Japanese and Manchurians, had passed into the employment of Manchoukuo, either directly or indirectly. Among them may be mentioned 1,396 police officers and men from the Japanese Embassy, 3,723 police officers and men from the Kwantung Bureau, 150 judicial officers postal officers and employees of the Kwantung Bureau, 340 tax office officers and employees, and 6,884 officers and employees of the Local Administration Bureau of the South Manchuria Railway Company. The last figure included an army of 2,663 teachers who were under the employment of the South Manchuria Railway Company and who had passed into the employment of the School Associations and Federation of School Associations.

Of the above mass transfer of personnel, the largest number naturally came from the South Manchuria Railway Company. On November 30, 1937, therefore, solemn ceremonies were held at Dairen and all other centers where the S.M.R. Local Administration Offices are located to bid an official farewell to the departing employees of the Company. And following this, the Local Administration Bureau of the South Manchuria Railway Company, with its thirty-year history of brilliant pioneership and achievement, had been dissolved.

The negotiations over various institutions which the South Manchuria Railway Company has maintained for experimental purposes, which were to be retained by the Company for the time being, had progressed smoothly after the above great transfer and a perfect understanding was reached between the South Manchuria Railway Company and the Manchoukuo Government by March, 1938. As a result, the second great transfer was made on April 1, 1938. It involved the following institutions: (1) the Kungchuling Agricultural Experimental Station; (2) the Hsiungyaocheng Agricultural Experimental Station; (3) the Yamuyingtzu Agricultural Experimental Station; (4) the Liaoyang Cotton Experimental Station; (5) the Fenghuangcheng Tobacco Experimental Station; (6) the Taonan Agricultural Experimental Station; (7) the Linshi Sheep Breeding Farm; (8) the Kungchuling Sheep Breeding Farm; (9) the Veterinary Institute; (10) the Geological Research Institute; (11) the Tunlenling Forestry Experimental Station; and (12) the Hsingcheng Horticultural Experimental Station. With the above, the Health Research Institute was transferred to the Kwantung Bureau and the Kwantung Army. These institutions which served as the basis of various industrial activities in the past were evaluated at 3,637,000 yen but were to be “loaned” to the authorities mentioned without compensation for the time being. With them, an additional number of 445 S.M.R. employees passed into the employment of Manchoukuo or the Kwantung Bureau.

Thus passed into history Japan's extraterritorial rights in Manchoukuo and her administrative rights over the S.M.R. Zone. It is to the credit of all parties concerned, their spirit of cooperation and careful preparations, that such an epochal transition of first magnitude was consummated with an amazing smoothness, even without a slightest hitch or difficulty. And the satisfactory result of the procedure has strongly underwritten Japan's trust placed upon Manchoukuo, as well as a phenomenal progress made in all phases of Manchoukuo's statehood during its short span of six years.

THE 1931 FLOOD IN CHINA

TABLE 2

POPULATION AND CULTIVATED AREA OF 131 FLOODED HSIEN
IN THE 1931 FLOOD AREA IN THE YANGTZE
AND HWAI VALLEYS, CHINA.*

| Province | Number of flooded hsien in the province included in the study | Total farm families affected (00 omitted) | Per cent. of cultivated area flooded | Cultivated area (mow) flooded (00 omitted) | Total farm families (00 omitted) | Total cultivated area (mow) (00 omitted) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Hunan | 15 | 4,242 | 51 | 89,634 | 9,088 | 174,059 |
| Hupeh | 30 | 10,227 | 55 | 139,183 | 19,919 | 253,427 |
| Kiangsi | 14 | 2,433 | 51 | 49,427 | 4,792 | 96,348 |
| South Anhwei | 24 | 6,132 | 62 | 86,797 | 9,906 | 140,227 |
| South Kiangsu | 11 | 2,243 | 43 | 40,255 | 5,375 | 93,675 |
| Honan | 1 | 636 | 85 | 31,875 | 748 | 37,500 |
| North Anhwei | 19 | 7,670 | 60 | 237,678 | 12,965 | 394,309 |
| North Kiangsu | 17 | 8,741 | 53 | 196,716 | 15,790 | 368,333 |
| Total | 131 | 42,324 | 56 | 871,565 | 78,583 | 1,557,878 |

*Most of the information on total farm families and total cultivated area per hsien is from data published under the direction of C. C. Chang of the former Statistical Bureau of the Legislative Yuan and from data collected in connection with the 1931 flood survey of The University of Nanking. Other sources were chiefly provincial government figures.

The percentages of cultivated area flooded are chiefly from estimates obtained from the 1931 flood survey of The University of Nanking and from planimetered data of land area flooded. Percentages from these two sources were checked with those obtained under the direction of C. C. Chang of the Directorate of Statistics and those reported by Magistrates to the National Flood Relief Commission, and with maps of area flooded.

For some hsien different sources gave great variation in the number of farm families and the amount of cultivated area. Determination of the more reasonable number was reached in part by computation of the density of population per square mile of cultivated area. Even the best figures give densities of great variation and often appear to be too high or too low. The average density of 1160 persons per square mile of cultivated area, for the entire area of the 131 hsien appears to be fairly reasonable as it checks with population densities previously obtained by the Department of Agricultural Economics, University of Nanking.

In cases of individual hsien, however, there may be serious underestimates of either number of families or of amount of cultivated area. For various reasons the amount of cultivated area is likely to be understated by at least 10-20 per cent.

tasks.output:
57

way Company to Manchoukuo from eleven cities and sixty-two towns and villages in the S. M. R. Zone alone were estimated at 31,438,994 yen and schools transfered to the Japanese authorities, 20,708,000 yen.

Together with this gigantic transfer, a total of nearly 14,000 persons, including Japanese and Manchurians, had passed into the employment of Manchoukuo, either directly or indirectly. Among them may be mentioned 1,396 police officers and men from the Japanese Embassy, 3,723 police officers and men from the Kwantung Bureau, 150 judicial officers, 1,500 postal officers and employees of the Kwantung Bureau, 340 tax office officers and employees, and 6,884 officers and employees of the Local Administration Bureau of the South Manchuria Railway Company. The last figure included an army of 2,663 teachers who were under the employment of the South Manchuria Railway Company and who had passed into the employment of the School Associations and Federation of School Associations.

Of the above mass transfer of personnel, the largest number naturally came from the South Manchuria Railway Company. On November 30, 1937, therefore, solemn ceremonies were held at Dairen and all other centers where the S. M. R. Local Administration Offices are located to bid an official farewell to the departing employees of the Company. And following this, the Local Administration Bureau of the South Manchuria Railway Company, with its thirty-year history of brilliant pioneership and achievement, had been dissolved.

The negotiations over various institutions which the South Manchuria Railway Company has maintained for experimental purposes, which were to be retained by the Company for the time being, had progressed smoothly after the above great transfer and a perfect understanding was reached between the South Manchuria Railway Company and the Manchoukuo Government by March, 1938. As a result, the second great transfer was made on April 1, 1938. It involved the following institutions: (1) the Kungchuling Agricultural Experimental Station; (2) the Hsiungyaocheng Agricultural Experimental Station; (3) the Yamuyingtzu Agricultural Experimental Station; (4) the Liaoyang Cotton Experimental Station; (5) the Fenghuangcheng Tobacco Experimental Station; (6) the Taonan Agricultural Experimental Station; (7) the Linhsi Sheep Breeding Farm; (8) the Kungchuling Sheep Breeding Farm; (9) the Veterinary Institute; (10) the Geological Research Institute; (11) the Tumenling Forestry Experimental Station; and (12) the Hsingcheng Horticultural Experimental Station. With the above, the Health Research Institute was transfered to the Kwantung Bureau and the Kwantung Army. These institutions which served as the basis of various industrial activities in the past were evaluated at 3,637,000 yen but were to be "loaned" to the authorities mentioned without compensation for the time being. With them, an additional number of 445 S. M. R. employees passed into the employment of Manchoukuo or the Kwantung Bureau.

Thus passed into history Japan's extraterritorial rights in Manchoukuo and her administrative rights over the S. M. R. Zone. It is to the credit of all parties concerned, their spirit of cooperation and careful preparations, that such an epochal transition of first magnitude was consummated with an amazing smoothness, even without a slightest hitch or difficulty. And the satisfactory result of the procedure has strongly underwritten Japan's trust placed upon Manchoukuo, as well as a phenomenal progress made in all phases of Manchoukuo's statehood during its short span of six years.

大阪市

△市勢 要覧

大阪の地は往古難波と呼ばる、海陸交通の要衝に位し神武天皇東征の際には征船をこの津に泊め給ふ、降つて仁徳天皇の高津宮御造営あり、隋唐との交通頻繁なるときには此地に鴻臚館を設けらる、その後豊公の築城成るに及んで商工業頗に興り近代大阪発展の端を開く、幾許もなくして冬夏両陣の兵禍を被り市民は離散したが、松平忠明の治領するや鋭意復興につとめ市街を整理し、水路を開鑿し大坂再生の基礎を定む徳川時代に入つてはその経済的発展はますます顕著で汎く海内の商権を握るに至り、また町人の都として文芸學術の方面にも異彩を放つた、明治22年市制實施により東西南北の4区を以て市域と定めたが、間もなく市域拡張の必要に迫られ明治30年4月1日、隣接28ヶ町村を合併す、さらに日露戦争及び世界大戦により市の経済力著しく増大し、市街地の膨脹もまた目覚しきものがあつたので、大正14年4月1日には第2次擴張を行ひ、東成、西成の2郡44ヶ町村を編入し行政区劃を13区に増した、かくて大阪市は今や人口250万を擁し、東洋第一の経済都市としての名實を

具へるに至つた、また畏くも今上陛下には特に産業御視察の思召で昭和4年6月4、5、6の3日間聖駕を大阪の地に駐めさせられ産業、教育その他の各種施設に臨幸を賜つたことは市史の上に永へに記念すべき光栄であ

POPULATION AND CULTIVATED AREA OF 131 FLOODED HSIEN
IN THE 1931 FLOOD AREA IN THE YANGTZE
AND HWAI VALLEYS, CHINA.*

| Province | Number of flooded hsien in the province included in the study | Total farm families affected (00 omitted) | Per cent. of cultivated area flooded | Cultivated area (mow) flooded (00 omitted) | Total farm families (00 omitted) | Total cultivated area (mow) (00 omitted) |

| Hupeh | 30 | 10,227 | 55 | 139,183 | 19,919 | 253,427 |

| South Kiangsu | 11 | 2,243 | 43 | 40,255 | 5,375 | 93,675 |
| Honan | 1 | 636 | 85 | 31,875 | 748 | 37,500 |
| North Anhwei | 19 | 7,670 | 60 | 237,678 | 12,965 | 394,309 |
| North Kiangsu | 17 | 8,741 | 53 | 196,716 | 15,790 | 368,333 |
| Total | 131 | 42,324 | 56 | 871,565 | 78,583 | 1,557,878 |

*Most of the information on total farm families and total cultivated area per hsien is from data published under the direction of C. C. Chang of the former Statistical Bureau of the Legislative Yuan and from data collected in connection with the 1931 flood survey of The University of Nanking. Other sources were chiefly provincial government figures.
The percentages of cultivated area flooded are chiefly from estimates obtained from the 1931 flood survey of The University of Nanking and from planimetered data of land area flooded. Percentages from these two sources were checked with those obtained under the direction of C. C. Chang of the Directorate of Statistics and those reported by Magistrates to the National Flood Relief Commission, and with maps of area flooded.
For some hsien different sources gave great variation in the number of farm families and the amount of cultivated area. Determination of the more reasonable number was reached in part by computation of the density of population per square mile of cultivated area. Even the best figures give densities of great variation and often appear to be too high or too low. The average density of 1160 persons per square mile of cultivated area, for the entire area of the 131 hsien appears to be fairly reasonable as it checks with population densities previously obtained by the Department of Agricultural Economics, University of Nanking.
In cases of individual hsien, however, there may be serious underestimates of either number of families or of amount of cultivated area. For various reasons the amount of cultivated area is likely to be understated by at least 10-20 per cent.

57

way Company to Manchoukuo from eleven cities and sixty-two towns and villages in the S.M.R. Zone alone were estimated at 31,438,994 yen and schools transferred to the Japanese authorities, 20,708,000 yen.

Together with this gigantic transfer, a total of nearly 14,000 persons, including Japanese and Manchurians, had passed into the employment of Manchoukuo, either directly or indirectly. Among them may be mentioned 1,396 police officers and men from the Japanese Embassy, 3,723 police officers and men from the Kwantung Bureau, 150 judicial officers, 1,500 postal officers and employees of the Kwantung Bureau, 340 tax office officers and employees, and 6,884 officers and employees of the Local Administration Bureau of the South Manchuria Railway Company. The last figure included an army of 2,663 teachers who were under the employment of the South Manchuria Railway Company and who had passed into the employment of the School Associations and Federation of School Associations.

Of the above mass transfer of personnel, the largest number naturally came from the South Manchuria Railway Company. On November 30, 1937, therefore, solemn ceremonies were held at Dairen and all other centers where the S.M.R. Local Administration Offices are located to bid an official farewell to the departing employees of the Company. And following this, the Local Administration Bureau of the South Manchuria Railway Company, with its thirty-year history of brilliant pioneership and achievement, had been dissolved.

The negotiations over various institutions which the South Manchuria Railway Company has maintained for experimental purposes, which were to be retained by the Company for the time being, had progressed smoothly after the above great transfer and a perfect understanding was reached between the South Manchuria Railway Company and the Manchoukuo Government by March, 1938. As a result, the second great transfer was made on April 1, 1938. It involved the following institutions: (1) the Kungchuling Agricultural Experimental Station; (2) the Hsiungyaocheng Agricultural Experimental Station; (3) the Yamuyingtzu Agricultural Experimental Station; (4) the Liaoyang Cotton Experimental Station; (5) the Fenghuangcheng Tobacco Experimental Station; (6) the Taonan Agricultural Experimental Station; (7) the Linhsi Sheep Breeding Farm; (8) the Kungchuling Sheep Breeding Farm; (9) the Veterinary Institute; (10) the Geological Research Institute; (11) the Tumenling Forestry Experimental Station; and (12) the Hsingcheng Horticultural Experimental Station. With the above, the Health Research Institute was transferred to the Kwantung Bureau and the Kwantung Army. These institutions which served as the basis of various industrial activities in the past were evaluated at 3,637,000 yen but were to be "loaned" to the authorities mentioned without compensation for the time being. With them, an additional number of 445 S.M.R. employees passed into the employment of Manchoukuo or the Kwantung Bureau.

Thus passed into history Japan's extraterritorial rights in Manchoukuo and her administrative rights over the S.M.R. Zone. It is to the credit of all parties concerned, their spirit of cooperation and careful preparations, that such an epochal transition of first magnitude was consummated with an amazing smoothness, even without a slightest hitch or difficulty. And the satisfactory result of the procedure has strongly underwritten Japan's trust placed upon Manchoukuo, as well as a phenomenal progress made in all phases of Manchoukuo's statehood during its short span of six years.

\*Most of the information on total farm families and total cultivated area per *hsien* is from data published under the direction of C. C. Chang of the former Statistical Bureau of the Legislative Yuan and from data collected in connection with the 1931 flood survey of The University of Nanking. Other sources were chiefly provincial government figures.

The percentages of cultivated area flooded are chiefly from estimates obtained from the 1931 flood survey of The University of Nanking and from planimetered data of land area flooded. Percentages from these two sources were checked with those obtained under the direction of C. C. Chang of the Directorate of Statistics and those reported by Magistrates to the National Flood Relief Commission, and with maps of area flooded.

For some *hsien* different sources gave great variation in the number of farm families and the amount of cultivated area. Determination of the more reasonable number was reached in part by computation of the density of population per square mile of cultivated area. Even the best figures give densities of great variation and often appear to be too high or too low. The average density of 1160 persons per square mile of cultivated area, for the entire area of the 131 *hsien* appears to be fairly reasonable as it checks with population densities previously obtained by the Department of Agricultural Economics, University of Nanking.

In cases of individual *hsien*, however, there may be serious underestimates of either number of families or of amount of cultivated area. For various reasons the amount of cultivated area is likely to be understated by at least 10-20 per cent.

english-page.png.text:
57

way Company to Manchoukuo from eleven cities and sixty-two towns and villages in the S. M. R. Zone alone were estimated at 31,438,994 yen and schools transfered to the Japanese authorities, 20,708,000 yen.

Together with this gigantic transfer, a total of nearly 14,000 persons, including Japanese and Manchurians, had passed into the employment of Manchoukuo, either directly or indirectly. Among them may be mentioned 1,396 police officers and men from the Japanese Embassy, 3,723 police officers and men from the Kwantung Bureau, 150 judicial officers, 1,500 postal officers and employees of the Kwantung Bureau, 340 tax office officers and employees, and 6,884 officers and employees of the Local Administration Bureau of the South Manchuria Railway Company. The last figure included an army of 2,663 teachers who were under the employment of the South Manchuria Railway Company and who had passed into the employment of the School Associations and Federation of School Associations.

Of the above mass transfer of personnel, the largest number naturally came from the South Manchuria Railway Company. On November 30, 1937, therefore, solemn ceremonies were held at Dairen and all other centers where the S. M. R. Local Administration Offices are located to bid an official farewell to the departing employees of the Company. And following this, the Local Administration Bureau of the South Manchuria Railway Company, with its thirty-year history of brilliant pioneership and achievement, had been dissolved.

The negotiations over various institutions which the South Manchuria Railway Company has maintained for experimental purposes, which were to be retained by the Company for the time being, had progressed smoothly after the above great transfer and a perfect understanding was reached between the South Manchuria Railway Company and the Manchoukuo Government by March, 1938. As a result, the second great transfer was made on April 1, 1938. It involved the following institutions: (1) the Kungchuling Agricultural Experimental Station; (2) the Hsiungyaocheng Agricultural Experimental Station; (3) the Yamuyingtzu Agricultural Experimental Station; (4) the Liaoyang Cotton Experimental Station; (5) the Fenghuangcheng Tobacco Experimental Station; (6) the Taonan Agricultural Experimental Station; (7) the Linhsi Sheep Breeding Farm; (8) the Kungchuling Sheep Breeding Farm; (9) the Veterinary Institute; (10) the Geological Research Institute; (11) the Tumenling Forestry Experimental Station; and (12) the Hsingcheng Horticultural Experimental Station. With the above, the Health Research Institute was transfered to the Kwantung Bureau and the Kwantung Army. These institutions which served as the basis of various industrial activities in the past were evaluated at 3,637,000 yen but were to be "loaned" to the authorities mentioned without compensation for the time being. With them, an additional number of 445 S. M. R. employees passed into the employment of Manchoukuo or the Kwantung Bureau.

Thus passed into history Japan's extraterritorial rights in Manchoukuo and her administrative rights over the S. M. R. Zone. It is to the credit of all parties concerned, their spirit of cooperation and careful preparations, that such an epochal transition of first magnitude was consummated with an amazing smoothness, even without a slightest hitch or difficulty. And the satisfactory result of the procedure has strongly underwritten Japan's trust placed upon Manchoukuo, as well as a phenomenal progress made in all phases of Manchoukuo's statehood during its short span of six years.

## 大阪市

### △市勢概觀

大阪の地は往古難波と呼ばる、海陸交通の要衝に位し神武天皇東征の際には征船をこの津に泊め給ふ、降つて仁德天皇の高津宮御造營あり、隋唐との交通頻繁なるときには此地に鴻臚館を設けらる、その後豐公の築城成るに及んで商工業頓に興り近代大阪發展の端を開く、幾許もなくして冬夏兩陣の兵禍を被り市民は離散したが、松平忠明の治領するや鋭意復興につとめ市街を整理し、水路を開鑿し大阪再生の基礎を定む、德川時代に入つてはその經濟的發展はます〳〵顯著で汎く海內の商權を握るに至り、また町人の都として文藝學術の方面にも異彩を放つた、明治22年市制實施により東西南北の4區を以て市域と定めたが、間もなく市域擴張の必要に迫られ明治30年4月1日、隣接28ケ町村を合併す、さらに日露戰爭及び世界大戰により市の經濟力著しく增大し、市街地の膨脹もまた目覺しきものがあつたので、大正14年4月1日には第2次擴張を行ひ、東成、西成の2郡44ケ町村を編入し行政區劃を13區に增した、かくて大阪市は今や人口250萬を擁し、東洋第1の經濟都市としての名實を具へるに至つた、また畏くも今上陛下には特に產業御視察の思召で昭和4年6月4、5、6の3日間聖駕を大阪の地に駐めさせられ產業、敎育その他の各種施設に臨幸を賜つたことは市史の上に永へに記念すべき光榮である。
